_readme: EDITORIAL RULINGS THAT OVERRIDE THE POWO EXPORT.
House rule, stated 2026-08-31: a published journal article trumps POWO.
The POWO export is the base list, not the verdict. Where Aroidpedia has
decided otherwise, the decision lives here and the extractor applies it.
exclude  a name POWO accepts that we do not. Dropped from the data.
include  a name POWO has dropped (or never carried) that we keep.
Needs a year, because it is not coming from the export.

mergeInto  on an `exclude`: the excluded name is a SYNONYM of this accepted name, so its distribution records transfer to it rather than being dropped. Added 2026-09-07 for Scindapsus rupestris; without it a synonymy silently shrinks the accepted species' range.
`authority` records whose ruling it is. A CITATION IS NOT REQUIRED --
user ruling 2026-09-01. These are Aroidpedia's own editorial calls and
stand on that; the checker does not ask for a source.
Consumed by scripts/extract-species-years.py, which prints every ruling
it applied and FAILS if one no longer matches -- if POWO starts listing
an `include` or drops an `exclude`, the run stops and names the entry, so
a ruling cannot quietly rot after POWO catches up.
Keys are genus slugs, lowercase.

STANDING RULE (owner, 2026-09-07): POWO RETAINS PRECEDENCE OVER VERY OLD PROTOLOGUES AND REDUCTIONS. 'A published journal article trumps POWO' is not mechanical - it weighs the article. A modern revision may displace the checklist (Hay & Yuzammi 2000 did, for Scindapsus rupestris); a very old reduction that no later worker has tested does not (Furtado 1935, Ridley 1907 and 1925, Engler & Krause 1908 did not). Such a reduction is NOT recorded as a ruling here, because nothing overrides the export - but it MUST be mentioned in the notes of every affected species, on BOTH sides of the pair, so the paper cannot resurface as an open question.
range    (added 2026-09-23) an accepted name whose NATIVE places a paper narrows or corrects.
`places` REPLACES POWO's list for that species in docs/genus-geo.json; every place must
already be in the genus's region tree or the builder refuses it. Introduced ranges are
never ruled here - naturalized populations go in page prose only (owner, 2026-09-23).
Applied by build-genus-geo 1.27.0; the builder says when POWO has caught up.

exclude.name: Scindapsus rupestris
exclude.reason: = Scindapsus sumatranus. Hay & Yuzammi 2000 (Telopea 9(1): 1-177) exclude Schismatoglottis sumatrana Schott ex Miq. from Schismatoglottis and recombine it as Scindapsus sumatranus (Miq.) P.C.Boyce & A.Hay (p. 170), and their Abstract (p. 1) states flatly that Scindapsus rupestris Ridl. is a synonym of it; the index (p. 177) sets Scindapsus rupestris in italic with a roman page number, which by that index's own legend marks a synonym rather than a formal treatment. POWO accepts both names. Under the house rule that a published journal article trumps POWO, Aroidpedia follows the paper. NOTE the p. 170 discussion itself is hedged ('the epithet is evidently an earlier one for Scindapsus rupestris Ridl.') and the authors could not find the type of the basionym, inferring the placement from Schott's Icones 3082; the ruling rests on the Abstract and index, which are unambiguous.
exclude.authority: Aroidpedia editorial, 2026-09-07 (owner ruling: 'go with Hay and Yuzammi')
exclude.mergeNote: A synonymy, not a deletion. POWO files four places under the synonym (Borneo, Peninsular Malaysia, Sumatra, Thailand) against one for the accepted name (Sumatra), so the distribution must transfer or Scindapsus sumatranus would be reduced to a one-island range for a taxon Hay & Yuzammi call 'widespread in West Malesia'. After the transfer the genus map keeps all 26 places; only Sumatra's species count falls (11 to 10), because it is the one place that counted both names.

exclude.name: Alloschemone inopinata
exclude.reason: = Alloschemone occidentalis. Hay, da Costa Soares & Gorfer 2025 (Aroideana 48(1): 1-16) place Alloschemone inopinata Bogner & P.C.Boyce in synonymy, 'synon. nov.' (p. 13): both characters of the 2001 protologue fail in material of Alloschemone occidentalis, and 'we therefore think it preferable to regard Alloschemone as monotypic' (p. 10). POWO accepts both names.
exclude.authority: Aroidpedia editorial, 2026-09-23 (owner ruling: 'if the paper is 2000+ then go with the paper')
exclude.mergeNote: Alloschemone inopinata carries only Brazil North, which Alloschemone occidentalis already holds; the genus map does not change, the count falls 2 -> 1.

exclude.name: Cryptocoryne jacobsenii
exclude.reason: = Cryptocoryne ×decus-silvae. Jacobsen, Wongso & Ørgaard 2023 (Aroideana 46(3): 1-23) list Cryptocoryne jacobsenii de Wit under Cryptocoryne ×decus-silvae de Wit [emend. N.Jacobsen et al. 2020], the hybrid Cryptocoryne cordata var. cordata × Cryptocoryne nurii (p. 14). POWO accepts Cryptocoryne jacobsenii.
exclude.authority: Aroidpedia editorial, 2026-09-23 (owner ruling: 'if the paper is 2000+ then go with the paper')
exclude.mergeNote: The target is written without the × because genus-geo keys species by POWO's bare epithet. POWO files Sumatra under Cryptocoryne jacobsenii and it transfers, as every merge does; the paper itself places only the type, cultivated ex Peninsular Malaysia.

range.name: Cryptocoryne cordata
range.reason: Jacobsen, Wongso & Ørgaard 2023 (Aroideana 46(3): 1-23) restore Cryptocoryne cordata to the diploid (2n = 34): southernmost Thailand, Peninsular Malaysia and, as var. wellyi, Sumatra. The Bornean plants are Cryptocoryne grabowskii, which already carries Borneo; Java is not part of the complex.
range.authority: Aroidpedia editorial, 2026-09-23 (owner ruling: 'if the paper is 2000+ then go with the paper')

range.name: Cryptocoryne siamensis
range.reason: Jacobsen, Wongso & Ørgaard 2023 (Aroideana 46(3): 1-23): the hexaploid (2n = 102) Cryptocoryne siamensis is southern and eastern Thailand and southwestern Cambodia, with var. diderici in Sumatra. No Peninsular Malaysian plant is claimed.
range.authority: Aroidpedia editorial, 2026-09-23 (owner ruling: 'if the paper is 2000+ then go with the paper')

range.name: Xanthosoma daguense
range.reason: Croat, Delannay & Hannon 2017 (Aroideana 40(2): 4-503): Xanthosoma daguense 'has been found so far only in Colombia' (Cauca, Chocó, Valle del Cauca, 0-460 m); the Ecuadorian material is Xanthosoma reticulatum and Xanthosoma rimbachii (pp. 22, 151).
range.authority: Aroidpedia editorial, 2026-09-23 (owner ruling: 'if the paper is 2000+ then go with the paper')

range.name: Xanthosoma undipes
range.reason: Croat, Delannay & Hannon 2017, Part 1 (Aroideana 40(2): 4-503): a species 'restricted to Costa Rica and Panama' (p. 7); Grayum's 2003 extension to Ecuador and Venezuela is rejected and those specimens are new species, the Puerto Rican plant being Xanthosoma acevedoi. Part 2 (Croat, Delannay & Ortiz 2017, 504-581) gives 'Nicaragua to Panama' (p. 565).
range.authority: Aroidpedia editorial, 2026-09-23 (owner ruling: 'if the paper is 2000+ then go with the paper')
